subject: Effect of scaling affects significance in joint Poisson model

messages.author: 1d4257855d4aabc6
messages.subject: Effect of scaling affects significance in joint Poisson model
parts:
Dear list

My background is the joint analysis of four indicators for a target measure which is impossible to determine. The four indicators are all counts of certain properties but with different means and variance. We have observed the four indicators in grouped subjects.
I started to analyse this using a poisson GLMM just with all counts of the four indicators concatenated. However, I realised that the different means and variances are a problem. I could however get roughly similar distributions by dividing the original indicator values by their mean.
Second option is the use of a joint INLA model with four Poisson response variables. However, in a simulation example this standardisation completely messes up my significance in INLA. On the other hand, both INLA results agrees with the GLMM.
I am not a bit worried what really the right way of analysing is? Is it GLMM with standardisation, which suggests the treatment effect is not significant, OR is it INLA without standardisation, which suggests a significant treatment effect. Hope this gets clearer with the example:

##Start of code
#Generating dataset
set.seed(1234)
fixEff <- 0.1
fixInt <- 3
EffInd <- rnorm(4,fixEff,0.1)
IntInd <- rnorm(4,fixInt,1.5)
GrInt <- sapply(IntInd, function(x) rnorm(9, x, .1))
SubjInt <- rnorm(180, 0, .01)
logl <- rep(GrInt, each=20) + SubjInt + rep(rep(c(0,1), each=10),36)*rep(EffInd, each=180)
ysim <- sapply(exp(logl), function(x) rpois(1, lambda=x))
d3 <- data.frame(ysim = ysim, Subj=rep(1:180,4), Ind=rep(LETTERS[1:4], each=180),
            Gr =rep(letters[1:9],each=20), Treat=rep(rep(c(0,1), each=10),36))
d3$ysimS <- d3$ysim/rep(tapply(d3$ysim, d3$Ind, mean),each=180)

##Generating stacked Y for INLA (original and standardized)
Y <- Ys <- matrix(NA, 180*4, 4)
E <- rep(1, 180*4)
for(i in 1:4) Y[(1:180)+((i-1)*180), i] <- d3$ysim[(1:180)+((i-1)*180)]
for(i in 1:4) Ys[(1:180)+((i-1)*180), i] <- d3$ysimS[(1:180)+((i-1)*180)]

formula <- Y ~ 1 + Treat + f(Gr, model="iid") + f(Subj, model="iid")
M1 <- inla(formula, data=d3, family=rep("poisson",4), E=E)
summary(M1)
#Significant treatment effect

formula <- Ys ~ 1 + Treat + f(Gr, model="iid") + f(Subj, model="iid")
M1S <- inla(formula, data=d3, family=rep("poisson",4), E=E)
summary(M1S)

M2 <- lmer(ysim ~ 1 + Treat + (1|Subj) + (1|Gr), data=d3, family="poisson")
summary(M2)
#Significant treatment effect in agreement with INLA.

M2S <- lmer(ysimS ~ 1 + Treat + (1|Subj) + (1|Gr), data=d3, family="poisson")
summary(M2S)
##End of code.

My original model was M2 of which I was suspicious because my indicator with largest mean showed strongest treatment effect. However, maybe this is effectively a true effect.
OR: My INLA specification is not entirely correct and I can do something better.

Any comments and thoughts are highly appreciated.
Kind regards
Manuel
